fields.title: Don't Just Build It, Understand It! Movie Recommendation System Explained | Python + ML
fields.description: Complete line-by-line breakdown of a Movie Recommendation System project: Content-Based Filtering, Data Preprocessing, TF-IDF Vectorization, Cosine Similarity, and Streamlit deployment.
fields.important_topics: Content-Based Filtering, TF-IDF Vectorization, Cosine Similarity, Streamlit UI, TMDB API
fields.quick_summary: Content-based recommendation systems extract feature vectors from metadata using TF-IDF and compute pairwise cosine similarity scores to recommend the top N closest items to a user selection.
fields.topic_flow: Recommendation Overview, Content-Based Filtering, TF-IDF Math, Cosine Similarity, Streamlit App

fields.title: Linear Regression in Machine Learning: Loss Function & Gradient Descent
fields.description: Learn how linear regression models continuous relationships, formulates the Mean Squared Error (MSE) cost function, and minimizes loss using gradient descent.
fields.important_topics: Linear Hypothesis, MSE Cost Function, Gradient Descent, Learning Rate
fields.quick_summary: Linear Regression finds the optimal line that minimizes the sum of squared differences between predicted values and actual observations using iterative gradient updates.
fields.topic_flow: Problem Formulation, Hypothesis Function, Loss Calculation, Gradient Update

fields.title: Ordinary Least Squares & Best Fit Line Calculation
fields.description: Master the mathematical derivation of the Ordinary Least Squares line of best fit, slope, intercept, and R-squared variance explanation.
fields.important_topics: Sum of Squared Residuals, Analytical Slope and Intercept, Covariance and Variance, R-Squared
fields.quick_summary: Ordinary Least Squares analytically computes the optimal slope and intercept that minimizes the total residual sum of squares without requiring iterative optimization.
fields.topic_flow: Residual Definition, Minimizing Squared Residuals, Closed-Form Solution, Goodness of Fit

fields.title: Categorical Data Types in ML: Nominal, Ordinal, and Binary Feature Encoding
fields.description: Understand the distinctions between nominal, ordinal, and binary categorical variables and choose the appropriate encoding technique (One-Hot vs Label Encoding).
fields.important_topics: Nominal Data, Ordinal Data, Binary Features, One-Hot vs Label Encoding
fields.quick_summary: Different categorical data types require distinct preprocessing: ordinal features preserve ranking order, while nominal features use one-hot encoding to avoid false numerical relationships.
fields.topic_flow: Categorical vs Numerical, Nominal Encoding, Ordinal Preservation, Dimensionality Trade-offs
